Another day, another LeBron James milestone.

The Philadelphia 76ers superstar notched 11 assists on Sunday in a 131-124 win over the Indiana Pacers, bringing his career total to 12,092 and surpassing Jason Kidd for the third most in NBA history. Not too shabby for the player who also has the most points in league history.

"It's super humbling. It's something that I didn't obviously foresee in my career," James told reporters after the victory. "But I knew assists meant a lot to me. Just the movement of the ball, being able to find my teammates and put the ball on time and on target."

James, 41, has always been an elite playmaker, but he's leaned heavily into the role in Philadelphia given the other offensive talent on the team. And while there were some questions about how James, Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown would all mesh despite just one basketball out on the court, the team has raced out to an 11-3 start.

And that is due, in part, to James' elite playmaking.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Stays Hot as Lakers Beat Suns, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Booker, Top Players
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers were without Austin Reaves on Sunday as he recovers from a bruise heel. But Luka Dončić picked up the slack and then some.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers were without Austin Reaves on Sunday as he recovers from a bruise heel. But Luka Dončić picked up the slack and then some.

The Lakers superstar put up 43 points, leading his team to a 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

It looked as though the Lakers were going to roll to an easy victory on Sunday, taking a 24-point lead into the fourth quarter and leading the contest by as many as 31 points. Dončić was cooking, per usual.

But the Suns came roaring back in the fourth, outscoring the Lakers 43-27 in the frame to make things interesting.

At one point, a frustrated Dončić even grabbed the coaching whiteboard to school up his teammates. Whether that worked or not is unclear, but the Lakers did manage to hold off Phoenix's furious comeback bid.

For the new-look Lakers, the 2026-27 season couldn't have gotten off to much better of a start. Los Angeles is now an NBA-best 12-2 on the season and Dončić is playing at an NBA level, surrounded by a cast of teammates hand-picked to complement his skill set. Thus far, it's jelling nicely.

The Suns, meanwhile, were a surprise playoff team last season but are just 5-7 this year and already popping up in trade rumors. They showed good fight on Sunday, but the 2026-27 season hasn't gone to plan thus far.

articles.title: Los Lakers casi tiran a la basura otra gran noche de Doncic
articles.standfirst: El base suma 42 puntos, pero los angelinos acaban pidiendo la hora tras ir 31 arriba (70-101)
articles.summary: El base suma 42 puntos, pero los angelinos acaban pidiendo la hora tras ir 31 arriba (70-101)
articles.body: A punto estuvieron los Lakers de tirar a la basura la enésima exhibición de Luka Doncic esta temporada. El base hizo 42 puntos (13/28 en tiros de campo y 5/13 en triples) y nueve asistencias, pero su equipo acabó pidiendo la hora después de marchar 31 arriba en el tercer cuarto (70-101). No es la primera vez que les sucede algo así a los Lakers. Amasan una buena renta al final del tercer cuarto y no la saben conservar cuando los titulares se marchan al banquillo con la intención de no volver... salvo que hay problemas. Y vaya si los hubo para ganar a los Suns (123-131) en la que fue la octava victoria consecutiva de los angelinos. Después de un partido discretísimo, los locales buscaron la remontada a la desesperada y casi les sale bien. Endurecieron su defensa hasta más allá de lo permitido y se la jugaron a triples. Lo que no les había entrado antes, les entraba en el último periodo, especialmente a Gillespie (26 puntos con 5/10 desde el arco). Koa Peat se colgaba varias veces del aro y, de repente, había partido: 104-116 con algo menos de siete minutos por jugar. Por entonces, Doncic llevaba 37 puntos en 29 minutos. Había hecho uno de esos partidos en los que el espectador se pregunta cómo ha llegado a esos números. Anota sin que te des cuenta, pero cuando lo haces tiene al rival desquiciado. Se había ido al banquillo y pensaba que ya no jugaría más, pero tuvo que volver a la pista para intentar arreglar el desaguisado. Salió frío e impreciso. Los Suns siguieron apretando y se colocaron a seis (111-117). Los Lakers no cogían un rebote y no dejaban de complicarse la vida con pérdidas absurdas y concediendo faltas de tres tiros. Tampoco los locales parecían querer ganar, pues perdonaron tres veces desde la línea de personal. Pese a ello, Gillespie ajustó el marcador un poco más, hasta el 121-126 con 1:05 por jugarse todavía. Ahí un rebote en ataque de Grimes y un posterior triple a tablero tras asistencia de Doncic resultarían decisivos cuando restaban 33 segundos. Él, con 22 puntos, fue el mejor escudero del esloveno en ausencia de Austin Reaves, aún de baja. Kessler hizo 14 puntos y 12 rebotes, aunque su incidencia en el choque fue de más a menos, Collin Sexton llegó a los 16 y Thybulle destacó en defensa. Gran contraste entre los titulares de los Lakers, todos en positivo en el +/-, y los suplentes, todos en negativo. Y al revés pasó en los Suns, cuyos suplentes metieron 78 puntos. Luke Kennard anotó 18 y Goodwin, 14. La estrella Devin Booker, que se sentó a falta de muchos minutos, hizo 17. Su entrenador prefirió jugarse el intento de remontada final con quienes habían dado esperanzas al equipo. Los angelinos alargan su racha y ya son ocho victorias consecutivas, las cuatro últimas a domicilio. Ahora les llegan Charlotte, Sacramento y Utah por partida doble. Citas, todas ellas en casa, propicias para mantener la progresión. Si es posible, con descanso para los referentes... y sin sobresaltos.

articles.body:
Assuming USC superstar JuJu Watkins declares for the 2027 WNBA draft, she's very likely headed to Canada.

The Toronto Tempo won the 2027 WNBA draft lottery on Sunday night after sharing the top odds (32.9%) to land the No. 1 pick this spring with the Houston Comets.

Here's a look at the full results and draft order as chalk held. The top seven picks were lottery selections.

Watkins is the prized jewel of this offseason's expected draft class. After missing the 2025-26 season due to a torn ACL she's returned in elite form, averaging 24.3 points, 8.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 3.7 steals while shooting 48.1 percent from the field.

Madison Booker is a pretty safe bet to be the No. 2 selection. The Texas forward is putting up 21.0 points, 4.3 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game this season, taking another nice step forward thus far in her senior season.

Barring a major change in play from either player, the WNBA draft will truly begin at No. 3, where players like Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo, LSU guard Mikaylah Williams and Virginia guard Kymora Johnson, among others, will make their case to fly off the board.

And given all of the time between now and April, plenty of other players will have a chance to jump up the board as well. But don't be surprised if Watkins and Booker are ultimately the first two names called.

articles.title: No. 7 Louisville rolls over No. 4 UConn in stifling 69-51 win
articles.summary: The uncharacteristically hapless Huskies were held to just 16 points in the first half on the way to a crushing loss.
articles.body:
The hits keep coming for No. 4 UConn: Less than two weeks after getting upset by Michigan, the Huskies fell to No. 7 Louisville on the road, in a 69-51 loss .

UConn's struggles were apparent early on, with the Huskies scoring only 16 first-half points — the lowest total under Huskies head coach Geno Auriemma since 2010, per ESPN.

Junior Cardinals guard Imari Berry had quite the night, scoring 11 points in the fourth quarter to grow Louisville's lead on the way to the 18-point win. Berry led both teams with 21 points, shooting 8 of 16 from the field, including five 3-pointers.

UConn forward Sarah Strong was held to 19 points — a relatively quiet night for the star junior — and the rest of the Huskies couldn't summon much of anything to fight back after going down early. At one point, Louisville was up by as many as 26 points; though UConn was able to cut into that deficit slightly, it was a shockingly one-sided matchup against the women's basketball mainstays.

The statement victory sets Louisville up for a rankings boost, as the Cardinals aced their first ranked matchup of the year.

For UConn, though, the emphatic loss raises some questions about the team as the Huskies continue a grueling early-season schedule. Unlike the Power Four programs, UConn, as part of the Big East, will have an easier conference schedule. However, the school has front-loaded its schedule with top opponents.

Under current women's basketball rankings, UConn is set to face nine top-25 opponents before Christmas. So far, the Huskies have faced four of those nine, going 2-2, and things won't slow down going forward: No. 1 South Carolina and No. 5 Duke are up later this month, with No. 19 Maryland, No. 12 Notre Dame and No. 9 LSU next month. (Those rankings are likely to change, with the new AP poll set to come out on Monday.)

articles.title: Luka Dončić scores 43, leading Lakers over Suns for eighth consecutive win, tying for NBA's top record
articles.summary: Dončić has scored 40 or more points in seven of the 12 games he's played this season.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić continued his scorching start to the 2026-27 NBA season, topping the 40-point mark for the seventh time in 12 games in the Los Angeles Lakers' 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns on Sunday. He currently leads the NBA in scoring at 38.6 points per game.

Dončić scored 20 of his 43 points in the first quarter, hitting three 3-pointers as he shot 5-for-10 and the Lakers took a 33-24 lead. That advantage increased to 54-37 with five minutes to go before halftime on a Jake LaRavia 3. Yet the Suns closed out the second quarter on a 12-3 run to trim the Lakers' lead to 61-54.

In the third quarter, the Lakers started hot from behind the arc, hitting three 3-pointers (two by Quentin Grimes) as part of a 13-3 run and boosted their lead to 20 points. Eventually, that margin became 31 points with under two minutes remaining in the quarter. Dončić added 12 points to put him at 37 points going into the final 12 minutes.

Phoenix recovered to give the Lakers a game in the fourth quarter, hitting four 3-point attempts to begin the frame. A Walker Kessler tip-in dunk restored the Lakers' advantage to 113-92 with just under nine minutes remaining.

However, the Suns responded with a 15-1 surge, fueled by six points from rookie Koa Peat. A 3 from Ryan Dunn cut the Lakers' lead to 117-111 at the 4:40 mark. Collin Gillespie drove to the basket for a layup that pulled Phoenix to within five points with 1:05 left in regulation.

But another 3 from Grimes effectively put the game away for the Lakers and Dončić closed out the scoring with two free throws. However, he told sideline reporter Roqui Theus afterward that the plan was for him to sit out the fourth quarter until the Suns made the game close.

"I wasn't planning on playing the fourth quarter," Dončić said. "We gotta get better at that. … Once we get up, we gotta stay there."

The Lakers played without Austin Reaves, who missed the game due to a bone bruise in his left heel .

Overall, Dončić shot 13-of-28 from the floor, while making 12-of-14 free throws. He also notched nine assists in his 43 minutes of play. Grimes followed with 22 points, shooting 5-for-6 on 3-pointers, with 6 assists and 2 steals. Collin Sexton contributed 16 points off the bench and Kessler added 14 points with 12 rebounds.

For the Suns, Gillespie finished with 26 points (shooting 5-for-10 on 3s), 4 assists and 4 rebounds. Luke Kennard added 18 as the Suns got 78 points from their reserves. Devin Booker led the Phoenix starters with 17 points and 7 assists.

The Lakers have won eight consecutive games and improved their record to 12-2, tying the San Antonio Spurs for the NBA's best record . (The Spurs defeated the Utah Jazz on Sunday, 110-102 .) Their next game is Tuesday versus the Charlotte Hornets (4-9).

articles.title: JJ Redick Doesn't Want to Put 'Ceiling' on Lakers' Potential After 8th Straight Win
articles.summary: It's still early in the 2026-27 campaign, but the Los Angeles Lakers have looked like one of the best teams in the NBA so far.
articles.body:
It's still early in the 2026-27 campaign, but the Los Angeles Lakers have looked like one of the best teams in the NBA so far.

After an eighth straight win, head coach JJ Redick doesn't want to put a ceiling on his group.

"I don't want these guys to put a ceiling on themselves," he said. "I don't think we should put a ceiling on this group. This group is committed to getting better every single day, recognizing that this is a process to become a high-level team and that's what I want for this group."

Many understandably expected the Lakers to take a step back after LeBron James left for the Philadelphia 76ers, but they've looked better than they did this time a year ago.

Their success is mostly because of Luka Dončić's historic start to the campaign. He's putting up 38.6 points, 7.6 assists and 7.5 boards per game, along with a pair of steals per game.

Austin Reaves has also been tremendous thus far, averaging 24.7 points per game, and the addition of Walker Kessler to the front court has been huge.

The Lakers are 12-2 and are tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the best record in the NBA. There are bound to be injuries and other setbacks, but Los Angeles has done nothing to indicate that it can't win it all this year.

articles.title: 2027 WNBA Mock Draft Predictions after Toronto Tempo Wins JuJu Watkins Lottery
articles.summary: The 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery has come and gone. The Toronto Tempo hold the first overall pick. Houston, Washington, Seattle, Portland, and Los Angeles (2x) round out the lottery order. Each of these teams will look to add a franchise-changing talent come April.
articles.body:
The 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery has come and gone. The Toronto Tempo hold the first overall pick. Houston, Washington, Seattle, Portland, and Los Angeles (2x) round out the lottery order. Each of these teams will look to add a franchise-changing talent come April.

While JuJu Watkins remains the projected No.1 overall selection, there are a handful of potential stars at the top of this draft. After the lottery, several prospects have strong chances to carve out impactful rotation roles in the league.

As NCAA action and international play continue to roll along, all of these players will look to cement their position as first-round talents. We won't know who's officially in the draft until early 2027, when most prospects declare, but for now, we'll assume that all eligible players are in the field. With that in mind, let's predict how every pick in the first round could shake out.

JuJu Watkins returned to the court after a year-long recovery from ACL surgery. She still looks like the best prospect in this draft. Despite a somewhat rough showing against No.1 South Carolina, no one should sell their Watkins stock; this is still a future WNBA MVP. Toronto is a great landing spot for Watkins, too. Her potential fit with Kiki Rice and Marina Mabrey is really fun to think about.

Watkins is an unreal two-way force, averaging 25 points per game and able to guard the opposing team's best player. Her tenacity and effort on defense are astounding for a player with such a large offensive load. Watkins is one of the better help defenders we've ever seen on the perimeter. She can legitimately protect the rim from the weak side.

Offensively, few players have the combination of handle, bag, and creativity that Watkins boasts. She can create any shot she wants. Her 6'2" size lets her shoot over most perimeter defenders. For all her offensive gifts, Watkins could improve as a three-point shooter and decision-maker. At times, she gets tunnel vision and ignores open teammates; this happened a lot against South Carolina. While Watkins isn't a bad shooter, her three-ball is still a pretty big question mark.

Watkins is not a perfect prospect. The flaws in her game could matter if she doesn't improve them at the pro level. That said, there isn't a single prospect who can match her two-way upside. If she hits her ceiling, she will go down as one of the greatest WNBA players of her generation. You take that player No.1 every single time.

2. Houston Comets: Madison Booker, Texas

In many drafts, Booker would be an easy No.1 pick. She has everything you want in a modern WNBA wing: size, length, shooting ability, ball-handling, playmaking, and defensive versatility. Booker is a potential superstar and a perfect franchise talent for Houston to pair with Leila Lacan.

Booker's best offensive skill is her midrange scoring. Her brilliance from that area rivals that of Courtney Williams or Paige Bueckers. She hit 47.7% of her pull-up twos last season (per Synergy). But like those players, Booker's midrange scoring can become a bit of a crutch. There's no reason to think that Booker can't become an elite three-point shooter; we just haven't seen that in Texas coach Vic Schaefer's three-suppressing system. Booker could also stand to put her head down and get to the basket more, because she's a good finisher and playmaker out of drives.

On defense, Booker can guard anyone on the perimeter. She's great at the point of attack, can hang with quick ball handlers, and she's big and long enough to defend wings. If she adds some muscle, she should be able to switch onto fours and fives, too. Booker has All-Defense potential. When you combine that with her plentiful offensive talents, you get a superstar worth building your franchise around.

3. Washington Mystics: Mikaylah Williams, LSU

Position: Shooting Guard/Wing, Size: 6'0", Age: 21

Williams is likely the best offensive player in this draft: a smooth three-level scorer with plus playmaking ability. LSU has played its typical cupcake non-conference schedule so far, but Williams has been on a tear to start this season, averaging 19 points and 5.5 assists per game on 68% true shooting. Williams is exactly what Washington needs. Her fit with Sonia Citron on the perimeter is a dream.

The shooting is what really sets Williams apart; she's automatic from everywhere. She can hit pull-ups from both two and three; she's great off the catch, and she finishes well at the rim. Williams's tight handle and good positional size allow her to get to her spots and create good shots out of nothing.

Williams is also a fantastic playmaker who can make advanced reads out of the pick-and-roll. While Williams isn't a true point guard and probably won't be able to hold up at the one in the WNBA, she's as good as it gets as a playmaking wing and secondary ball handler. A 6'0" player who can dribble, pass, and shoot is a potential star in today's game.

If Williams is to reach her ceiling, she'll need to improve on defense. She's not the best athlete and often struggles to stay in front of good perimeter creators. Her effort both on and off the ball can come and go. Williams' subpar athleticism also limits her as a driver. She doesn't get to the rim as often as you'd want from one of your top scoring options.

Even with those weaknesses, Williams is a tremendous prospect with a real case to go as high as No. 2 in this draft. Washington is a perfect scenario for Williams. They have the defensive infrastructure to insulate her. They can also develop Williams as a primary creator.

4. Seattle Storm: Hannah Hidalgo, Notre Dame

Position: Combo Guard, Size: 5'6", Age: 21

Hannah Hidalgo is having a typical Hannah Hidalgo start to this season, stuffing the stat sheet with averages of 28.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 4.8 steals through her first four games. Over the past 3+ years, you could argue that no player in college basketball has been better than Hidalgo. She contributes in so many areas on both ends of the floor. No one can match her relentless motor and desire to win. Seattle would be thrilled to get Hidalgo at No. 4 as a perfect complement to their talented young frontcourt.

Why isn't Hidalgo being discussed in No. 1 pick conversations? She has the production, the pedigree, and the two-way impact of a top prospect, after all. All that said, there are issues that make Hidalgo unique and a tricky evaluation at the top of the draft.

For starters, Hidalgo's 5'6" height works to her disadvantage. Players that small usually need to be good pull-up shooters to return elite offensive value. Hidalgo's jumper has been inconsistent and unreliable, especially from three. Here are Hidalgo's three-point percentages by year: 34%, 40%, 25%. This year, she's 6-for-15 (40%) so far. College season samples can be wonky, but it's hard to know if we can project Hidalgo as a good shooter in the WNBA. Hidalgo's handle is also mediocre. Her playmaking rarely goes beyond basic reads. If she can't play point guard full time, her offensive upside is a bit limited.

Defensively, Hidalgo is an elite point-of-attack menace and one of the most disruptive on-ball defenders of all time. She also plays much bigger than her size, with explosive vertical athleticism and intense physicality. Hidalgo should be a great defender in the league, but there are questions as to how much her size limits her against WNBA athletes. If Hidalgo is simply a good defender instead of an All-Defensive one, how high is her ceiling? Whoever drafts Hidalgo will have to weigh all of those outcomes.

5. Portland Fire: Clara Strack, Kentucky

Pro Comp: Dominique Malonga with less athleticism

Strack might not be the fifth-best prospect in this draft, but she's a perfect fit for what the Fire are building. The 6'5" big has enjoyed a strong start to her senior season, averaging 18.4 points, 9.6 rebounds, and 3.8 blocks through five games.

With the league valuing stretch bigs more than ever before, Strack is a tantalizing option for teams picking in the mid-to-late lottery. Strack's shooting has been largely theoretical throughout her college career, though she did put up a respectable 2.8 three-point attempts per game last season. This year, she's bumped that up a notch; Strack is 8-for-21 on threes so far. She's taking four per game. She missed her first seven attempts and is 8-for-14 since.

If Strack can reliably stretch the floor, her ceiling as a player would grow substantially. Strack is a bit of a "jack of all trades, master of none" player on offense. She's a decent screener and roller, not a great one. She can hit post fades and make some decent passes out of doubles, but she's not someone you can build a post-up offense around. Strack isn't quick or skilled enough with the ball to take defenders to the basket. So she really needs the three-point shooting to open up all of these other areas.

Strack can make a real impact on defense, though. She's the best rim protector in this draft class by a wide margin. Her mobility is good enough to hold up in non-drop coverages. If the offense comes together, Strack could be a good starter on competitive teams. Portland also has the developmental infrastructure and coaching to get the most out of Strack's talent.

6. Los Angeles Sparks: Tessa Johnson, South Carolina

Position: Shooting Guard, Size: 6'0", Age: 21

Every WNBA team could always use more three-point shooting. Johnson is as automatic as it gets as a spot-up threat. She's a career 43.9% shooter from deep in her time at South Carolina. That skill gives her one of the safest floors in this draft class. The Sparks were toward the bottom of the league in three-point shooting last season. Johnson would inject some offensive life into their young core.

Although shooting is the primary selling point for Johnson, she's not an entirely one-dimensional player. She has a strong pull-up middy to attack closeouts with. She's even flashed some driving ability here and there. Johnson also moves well without the ball and does a good job of cutting and relocating off screens. Her ceiling, however, is limited by a poor handle and burst and a complete lack of pull-up shooting from three. In her college career, Johnson has just 43 off-the-dribble three-point attempts, hitting 16 (37%). That's not a bad percentage, but the volume is alarmingly low.

Defensively, Johnson should be able to stay afloat as a solid team defender who plays with good physicality and awareness. But she does struggle a bit at the point of attack, where her slender frame and lack of quickness impede her against ball handlers. There are enough tools to avoid becoming a target on defense. The offensive value Johnson provides with her shooting gravity and movement should yield a positive overall impact.

7. Los Angeles Sparks (from Phoenix): MiLaysia Fulwiley, LSU

Position: Shooting Guard, Size: 5'10", Age: 21

If Fulwiley could put everything together, she might end up as the second-best player in this draft. She's that talented, with outlier skills that make it easy to overlook all of the question marks. The Sparks need upside in their guard room, so Fulwiley feels like the perfect player to take a swing on at the end of the lottery.

Fulwiley is a wizard with the basketball, equipped with one of the best handles in the game. Combined with her burst and athleticism, that gives Fulwiley special creation potential at either guard spot. Fulwiley is at her best in transition, where she can leverage her breakneck speed and ball skills to create easy opportunities in the open court.

The issue is that Fulwiley usually plays far too out of control. Through her first three college seasons, the game has yet to slow down for her. As a result, Fulwiley's decision-making often gets her into trouble. This affects her shot selection, playmaking, and finishing. There is no deceleration game to speak of. Fulwiley often predetermines what she'll do on drives instead of reading the defense. When she does get to the basket, she's a horrible finisher. Last year in half-court offense, Fulwiley was just 25-64 (39%) at the rim against P4 opponents (per Synergy). She's also an inconsistent shooter without much off-ball utility.

Even with the issues on offense, Fulwiley projects as a special defensive weapon. Her vertical athleticism is special, as she's one of the rare sub-6-foot players who can function as a legitimate secondary rim protector. Fulwiley is also a menace at the point of attack, preventing drives and creating turnovers with regularity. These skills give Fulwiley a decent floor as a change-of-pace energy guard, even if she doesn't figure things out in half-court offense.

Note: Fulwiley is involved in a pending legal incident that could affect her draft stock. This was written independently of that.

8. New York Liberty: Oluchi Okananwa, Maryland

Position: Guard/Wing, Size: 5'10", Age: 22

It can be tough to build around non-shooting two guards under six feet, but Okananwa has enough winning skills to work around those red flags. The Liberty have a ton of offensive firepower and could use a defensive-minded athlete like Okananwa to complement their core.

Okananwa is an elite point-of-attack defender with a relentless motor. The comparison to DiJonai Carrington is uncanny here, as both players play bigger than their size and wreck games on defense. In addition to her defensive prowess, Okananwa is the best offensive rebounding guard in college basketball. Last season, Okananwa posted an offensive rebound rate of 16.7%, 95th percentile in all of Division I (per Her Hoops Stats).

Offensively, there's less to be excited about. Okanawa's jumper doesn't go in. It looks bad, too. She's also not a very good passer; it's tough to envision Okanawa succeeding, even as a tertiary playmaker in the league. But Okanawa is a strong driver who gets to the free-throw line. Her rim finishing has improved, too: in 2024-2025, Okanawa converted just 45% of her rim attempts in the half-court (per Synergy Sports). Last year, that number jumped to 61%.

Okanawa had a rough showing in her first game of the season against No. 1 South Carolina, shooting 5-for-14. She bounced back with a strong performance against Georgia Tech, so hopefully she can build on that and secure a spot in the first round of this draft.

9. Dallas Wings: Chloe Kitts, South Carolina

Kitts returned to the floor after a year-long recovery from an ACL tear and hasn't missed a beat. The 6'2" forward is averaging 13 points and 10.2 rebounds per game through No. 1 South Carolina's first three contests on 52.9% shooting from the field. The Gamecocks have played three ranked opponents, making Kitts' early production all the more impressive.

There's nothing flashy about Kitts's game, but she's the kind of connective player who helps teams win. If you put a smaller player on her, she can post up and score. If you double the ball handler off a Kitts screen, she can catch the pass and find the open player. When a shot goes up, Kitts crashes the offensive glass. Kitts has a knack for stacking plays like this throughout a game.

Defensively, Kitts is incredibly versatile and smart. She has some of the best help instincts of anyone in this class and plays with tenacious physicality. While the athleticism leaves a lot to be desired, Kitts is mobile enough to switch and big enough to defend post players.

The swing skill for Kitts is her jump shooting. She doesn't take threes, as her form looks a bit wonky. However, Kitts shot 37-for-72 (51%) on two-point jumpers in her junior year, so there's hope she can expand her range and become a real shooter. If she does, she'll be a good role player for a long time. Dallas needs better frontcourt players who can guard. Kitts fits the bill.

10. Indiana Fever: Talaysia Cooper, Ole Miss

Cooper has had a very strange start to her season at Ole Miss. The Tennessee transfer got benched after a mediocre opening game and scored just 5 points on 2-10 shooting against North Alabama in game two. Then, one game later against Albany, Cooper exploded for 29 points and seven made three-pointers. Go figure!

Throughout her college career, Cooper's calling card has been her length and athleticism. She's an explosive player with quickness and strength who could be an impact defender at the next level. For all her athletic gifts, Cooper doesn't really get to the rim, finish or draw fouls. As a result, she's turned to three-point maxing as a way to return offensive value (.415 three-point rate last year and .600 so far this year).

Is Cooper a good shooter? Not really. The mechanics don't look great. The touch indicators and free-throw percentage (64% career) aren't encouraging. But there is value in being willing to take threes, and Cooper isn't shy. One thing to monitor this year: Cooper looks like she's added a good amount of muscle to her frame. Watching her first few games, she looks a good deal slower and less explosive than before. We'll see if that added strength helps her in other ways as the season goes on.

There's undeniable upside with Cooper. A team like Indiana could use stronger, athletic players on the wing. There's a good floor for Cooper as a versatile defender, but questions about her feel and offensive role could hold her back from breaking through in the league.

11. Chicago Sky (Washington Swap): S'Mya Nichols, Kansas

Position: Guard/Wing, Size: 6'0", Age: 22

Nichols is a prolific ball-screen operator with some of the craziest foul-baiting prowess of any prospect ever; her career .721 free-throw rate will raise the eyebrows of any talent evaluator. When she isn't barreling into the lane and getting whistles, Nichols leans on savvy playmaking with good vision and passing skills. In a league increasingly moving toward heavy pick-and-roll offense, Nichols' strengths are incredibly appealing.

So, what's the catch? Well, for starters, Nichols hasn't faced much elite competition in her college career. It's great to beat up on bad Big 12 teams and mid-majors in non-conference, but can Nichols get her game on against the sport's best? There's not enough data to know.

The ancillary skills are also a question mark. Nichols has great three-point shooting percentages, but she's only taken 246 threes in 102 college games. For an extreme high-usage guard who shoots 39%, that's alarmingly low. Nichols's jumper has a lot of moving parts and a slow release. She may struggle to shoot against WNBA players. Her two-point scoring is also suspect, because when she isn't getting to the line, she doesn't really score from anywhere else.

Nichols is also projected as a mediocre-to-bad defender. If she can't guard, can't score from two, and can't really shoot threes, what does she do in the W when she isn't running a bunch of ball screens? And is she good enough at that to build your offense around? These are all questions teams have to answer when considering Nichols. Chicago needs offensive talent at the guard spots, though, so they'd be a good team to roll the dice if she falls.

12: Chicago Sky (from Atlanta), Ashlyn Watkins, South Carolina

Like her teammate Kitts, Watkins is also returning from a torn ACL. Watkins, however, took nearly two years off from basketball before rejoining South Carolina this year. She's looked predictably rusty through three games and hasn't done much offensively, but there's still enticing upside.

Watkins is the best athlete in this draft class with an incredibly rare blend of verticality, quickness, and size. She's thrown down multiple in-game dunks, making it look easy. Those athletic tools make Watkins a fearsome defender who can play any coverage and anchor a defense.

But offensively, Watkins is a bit of a nothingburger; she's scored just seven total points in three games this year. She is coming off the bench, buried in the offensive pecking order, and working her way back from injury. But even with those caveats, Watkins projects as a below-average offensive player. There just aren't a lot of projectable skills on that end.

Despite those offensive concerns, Watkins will likely be drafted in the first round. The potential fit with Chicago is intriguing, as Watkins could act as a nice change-of-pace option behind fellow Gamecock Kamila Cardoso.

13. Dallas Wings (from Las Vegas): Kymora Johnson, Virginia

Position: Point Guard, Size: 5'7", Age: 21

You may be thinking, "another undersized guard for the Wings?" That sentiment is understandable, but Dallas has a hole at backup point guard. Odyssey Sims likely isn't coming back, and she didn't play well last year anyway. Enter Johnson, who has the point guard traits teams look for in the modern WNBA.

Well, most of them, anyway; Johnson is listed at 5'7". Though vertically challenged, Johnson is a terrific ball-screen operator who is looking to shoot threes first and find teammates later. She's better off the catch than pulling up (37% vs. 34% last year, per Synergy), but her career three-point shooting sample is legit. Johnson's playmaking is a solid complement to her score-first game, though she isn't a tier-one passer and can get a bit turnover-prone.

The most concerning thing about Johnson is her lack of rim pressure and finishing. Last year, just 19.5% of her field goal attempts in the half-court came at the rim. She finished at a ghastly 47% clip (per Synergy). The Wings desperately need guards who can get to the basket. Johnson is decidedly not that. But there aren't any players who can at this point in the draft, so penciling in Johnson to hold down the backup point guard spot is as good as they can hope for.

Johnson has been incredible to start the season, even if it's been against weaker mid-major teams. Her first big test will be on November 23rd against Oklahoma.

14. Golden State Valkyries: Sarah Cisse, France

The Valkyries add another baguette to the basket and expand their monopoly on French players here. Cisse, currently playing for BLMA in the top French league (La Boulangère Wonderligue), would be a compelling draft-and-stash piece for the reigning champs. She fits well with how they want to play. It's hard to imagine a better developmental context for the talented (but raw) big.

Cisse is an undersized 4/5 who is coasting on athleticism right now. BLMA has played some pretty poor teams in EuroCup competition recently. Cisse is feasting on mismatches, offensive rebounds, and post seals. All of that is great, but we'll see how she looks once she has to face the best of LBW.

A player of Cisse's build is always going to face tweener issues, so she really needs to add a somewhat reliable jumper to round out her offensive utility. Her form looks pretty good, though; she just needs to get more comfortable taking them.

Defensively is where Cisse will make her money. She possesses incredible lateral quickness and should be able to capably switch onto WNBA guards. Cisse's vertical athleticism and strength are also good enough to provide strong secondary rim protection. Her defensive ceiling is through the roof. That's worth drafting in the first round, even if the offense never really comes together.

Position: Point Guard, Size: 5'9", Age: 21

Arnold screams "prototypical WNBA backup point guard," and playing for Cheryl Reeve in the Minnesota system would be a perfect fit. You know what you're getting with Arnold: energy, pesky point-of-attack defense, smart passing, and the occasional drive-and-finish.

Sure, Arnold is never going to score 30 points in a game or make any All-Star teams. But there's a lot of value in a spark-plug guard who can defend, pass, and finish at the rim. If Arnold's three-point shooting improves, she might even grow into a positive offensive player. Through three games this season, Arnold is 4-for-10 from three, so the hope is she can keep up the volume and make them.

If the shot does start drawing closeouts, Arnold's passing and rim pressure will flourish. In that situation, this is the ideal backup guard, one that can make a Kaitlyn Chen-like impact or a title team. You could certainly do a lot worse with the very last pick of the first round.

articles.title: Trae Young Goes Scoreless in Wizards' Blowout Loss to Rockets, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: Oh no, Trae Young.
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards point guard was held scoreless in 26 minutes during his team's 147-119 loss against the Houston Rockets on Sunday. While he did manage eight assists, he added three turnovers, only attempted five field goals and was minus-28 in the contest.

It was Washington's seventh straight loss in what is rapidly going from an extremely promising and much-anticipated season to an abject disaster.

Asked what allowed him to score a season-high 25 points off the bench, Rockets forward Tari Eason said: "S--t, the Wizards, for real."

Everything was supposed to be different for Washington this year.

Young and Anthony Davis were going to give them an exciting one-two punch. AJ Dybantsa was drafted with the top overall pick. Players like Kyshawn George, Alex Sarr and Bilal Coulibaly had shown real promise early in their careers and rounded out a promising core.

Perhaps the five-year playoff drought—and nine-year streak without a playoff series win—would finally be coming to a close. At the very least, it was a reason for excitement, something Wizards fans haven't had much of since the peak of the John Wall and Bradley Beal years.

And there was promise—real, actual hope—after a 4-3 start. But it's all come crashing down, and fast.

Young has been erratic in the team's seven-game losing streak. He had a four-point game in a blowout loss against the Oklahoma City Thunder. His three-point shooting, in general, has been rough.

But he also put up 37 points and 14 assists in Thursday's double-overtime loss against the Detroit Pistons. He's been fantastic as a playmaker, averaging 7.4 assists per game during the losing streak (although that's below his average overall on the season).

Something just isn't clicking in the nation's capital. To a degree that's to be expected—the Wizards are a young team and Young and Davis haven't played together before. There was always going to be an adjustment period.

But Sunday's night was emblematic of just how rough the things have gotten. If the Wizards don't figure it out, and soon, it's going to be yet another trip to the lottery.

articles.title: LeBron James makes NBA history with 76ers teammates caught in the middle of his latest milestone celebration
articles.summary: LeBron James passed Jason Kidd for third place on the NBA’s all-time assists list in the Philadelphia 76ers’ 131-124 win over the Indiana Pacers at
articles.body: LeBron James passed Jason Kidd for third place on the NBA’s all-time assists list in the Philadelphia 76ers’ 131-124 win over the Indiana Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Sunday. The pass came with 1:19 left in the fourth quarter, a layup for VJ Edgecombe to make it 128-119. It was the 11th assist of the game for James and the 12,092nd of his career. The four-time champion finished with 15 points and joked afterward that teaching younger teammates the right timing has meant hitting a few of them in the head.How did LeBron James pass Jason Kidd on the all-time assists list?LeBron James needed to beat Jason Kidd’s career total of 12,091, and the layup for VJ Edgecombe did it. Only John Stockton (15,806) and Chris Paul (12,552) have more.The NBA’s all-time leading scorer gave the credit to others. “I had a lot of great teammates,” James said in the postgame television interview. The Philadelphia forward described the job as getting the ball there on time and on target, then sending teammates to the rim. Any spot on an NBA history list, James said, is an honor. James also called Kidd a dear friend and said sharing the list with him is special.Passing has been part of the game for James since rec league days, when watching a teammate score was the fun part. The 24th-year veteran also shot 5 of 8 from the field.Edgecombe and Maxey are learning James’ timingA reporter asked how teammates adjust to a playmaker who sees plays before they develop. “Hit them in the head a couple of times,” James said. Edgecombe was one of them. The second-year guard did not finish a route in practice early in training camp, and James told him to expect the ball even when he did not think he was open.Edgecombe, 21, was born in July 2005, nearly two years after James entered the league in 2003. The guard has joked about the 20-year gap, saying James is old enough to be his dad.Maxey already knows what is coming. The two have trained together for the last six summers. On one jump pass against Indiana, James stared at the rim, drew the defender’s eyes, and found Maxey on the left wing by the Pacers’ bench. Maxey told him he did not believe the pass was possible.Pacers coach Rick Carlisle has compared James to an AI machine built for basketball. James traced the trait to Little League, AAU ball and high school, where studying what opponents ran meant teammates got a read too.The 76ers are 11-3 and second in the East, and played this one without Joel Embiid, who is sidelined for right foot plantar fascia injury management. Jaylen Brown led the team with 31 points and Maxey added 27.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Might Be the Greatest Offensive Player Ever,’ ‘The MVP Season We’ve All Been Waiting For’ — NBA World Marvels As Luka Dončić’s Historic Start Continues
articles.summary: Luka Dončić poured in a game-high 43 points Sunday as the shorthanded Los Angeles Lakers held off the Phoenix Suns 131-123 on the road for their eighth strai...
articles.body:
Luka Dončić poured in a game-high 43 points Sunday as the shorthanded Los Angeles Lakers held off the Phoenix Suns 131-123 on the road for their eighth straight win.

That marked the superstar guard's seventh 40-point game in just 12 appearances this season. The eye-popping pace left the NBA world digging through the record books and further amplified the two-time scoring champion's early MVP buzz.

Luka Dončić's Wilt Chamberlain-Esque Start Earns High Praise

Dončić rolled his ankle in Wednesday's 123-112 road win over the Milwaukee Bucks but didn't miss a game or skip a beat. The six-time All-Star shot 13-for-28 overall (46.4%), 5-for-13 from long range (38.5%), and 12-for-14 from the free-throw line (85.7%) against Phoenix, adding 9 assists in 36 minutes.

Austin Reaves, LA's second-leading scorer (24.7 points per game), sat with a bruised heel sustained against Milwaukee, putting the onus on Dončić to carry his squad offensively.

LA led 101-70 late in the third quarter, but Phoenix rallied with a 43-27 edge in the final frame, cutting its deficit to 126-121 on a Collin Gillespie layup with 1:05 remaining.

Dončić answered by finding Quentin Grimes for a triple before closing out the game at the charity stripe. He vastly outperformed Suns star Devin Booker, who managed 17 points on 4-for-14 shooting (28.6%) and sat out the entire fourth quarter.

After Dončić's seventh 40-point night, which featured an array of tough shot-making, NBA on ESPN put his start in historical context, noting that he "trails only two Wilt Chamberlain seasons for the most through a player's first 12 games."

NBA content creator Six Rings of Steel focused on the winning that has accompanied Dončić's historic scoring pace. The 27-year-old has guided the Lakers to a league-best-tying 12-2 record while averaging a career-high 39.0 ppg on elite 48.6/40.6/86.5 shooting splits.

"This is truly one of the most insane scoring/winning starts to the season we've ever seen," Six Rings of Steel raved.

Fellow content creator Biased Houston took the praise a step further, suggesting, "Luka Dončić might be the greatest offensive player ever, man. We are reaching these waters."

The offensive mastery behind those numbers was on display from the opening tip, as Dončić piled up 20 points in a first quarter the Lakers won 33-24. He scored or assisted on each of their first 10 points and buried a deep 3-pointer for a 23-5 lead.

Yahoo Sports' Steve Jones put it simply, questioning, "What is wrong with Luka Dončić?"

"Luka Dončić with another 40+ point game tonight after a short break with back-to-back 32-point games. Crazy how he makes things look even easier now that he's learned the [Nikola] Jokić lesson," Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor added.

Others went straight to the MVP conversation. Basketball Performances declared, "He's finally putting together the MVP season we've all been waiting for."

Lakers fan page LakeShowYo was more direct, stating, "Luka is the MVP, argue with your momma."

Dončić will look to keep the magic alive when the Lakers (12-2) host the Charlotte Hornets (4-9) on Tuesday to open a four-game homestand.

articles.title: LeBron James says he’s just done something he never thought he would do in his career
articles.summary: LeBron James continues to make history in his 24th season in the NBA. The 41-year-old started for the Philadelphia 76ers in their 131-124 win against the Ind...
articles.body:
LeBron James continues to make history in his 24th season in the NBA.

The 41-year-old started for the Philadelphia 76ers in their 131-124 win against the Indiana Pacers on Sunday, and The King was in great form.

James recorded 11 assists against the Pacers, and that took him past an iconic name in the all-time NBA assists charts. He says he never saw that coming.

LeBron James says he didn't foresee ranking third on the NBA career assists list

James is one of the most complete players the NBA has ever seen.

Over the course of his 24-year-long career, the four-time champion has played in all five positions on the court, and he has amassed incredible numbers under every metric.

On Sunday, James took his career assists tally to 12,092, surpassing Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd to rank third on the list.

That is an incredible achievement, one James says he is humbled by, but he has revealed that he never foresaw achieving this in his career.

He said: "It's super humbling. It's something that I didn't obviously foresee in my career. But I knew assists meant a lot to me. Just the movement of the ball, being able to find my teammates and put the ball on time and on target.

"And also just being linked with some of the greats to have ever played this game, and also a dear friend of mine, J Kidd, is really special."

James now ranks third on the all-time assists list, below leader John Stockton, who recorded 15,806 career assists, and Chris Paul, who assisted 12,552 times.

Ironically, James was on the Redeem Team of 2008 along with Kidd and Paul. He has overtaken one, and it now remains to be seen if he can do the same to the other before the end of this season.
