articles.title: Power Ranking Every NBA Team's Starting Lineup So Far
articles.summary: We haven't quite hit the one-month mark of the 2026-27 NBA campaign, but it's not too early to take stock of how every team is starting games.
articles.body:
We haven't quite hit the one-month mark of the 2026-27 NBA campaign, but it's not too early to take stock of how every team is starting games.

Plenty of teams have already been forced into multiple different starting lineups. Some have looked more stable. Injuries have affected just about everyone.

For consistency, we're using each team's most-used starting five, rather than its current lineup or its projected starting five entering the season.

That will give us bigger samples to analyze. And in several cases, we'll acknowledge that the lineup on the board may not be the one that ends up leading the way for its team.

From there, based on numbers like point differential and win-loss record, and with a healthy dose of subjectivity (which could include 2025-26 performance) and anticipation for how they'll perform going forward, we ranked every team's most-used starting lineup so far.

Numbers courtesy of NBA.com/stats, Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass and current through November 14, 2026.

30. Utah Jazz: George, Peterson, Bailey, Markkanen, Hayes

In every season since they traded Rudy Gobert and Donovan Mitchell, injuries have been an underlying theme for the Utah Jazz. And that applies to 2026-27, when they were supposed to finally turn a corner.

Not even a month into this campaign, Utah has already deployed six different starting lineups. Keyonte George (20.9 points and 6.5 assists), Lauri Markkanen (18.0 points and 6.8 rebounds) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (16.3 points and 1.3 blocks) have all already missed time. And Ace Bailey (13.9 points, while shooting 27.3 percent from three), at least on the offensive end, hasn't really taken the leap.

On the bright side, in the wake of the injuries, rookie Darryn Peterson has come alive. Over his last five games, he's averaged 24.4 points and 4.0 assists, while shooting 38.6 percent from deep.

29. Chicago Bulls: Giddey, Powell, Buzelis, Wilson, Smith

An injury to Nicolas Claxton has prevented the Chicago Bulls from using their anticipated starting five even once this season. And now that Caleb Wilson is out with a broken hand, we're going to have to wait even longer to see it.

But 80 percent of Chicago's starters have spent plenty of time together. And the whole group's terrible numbers are hardly the fault of Claxton's substitute. Jalen Smith actually leads the Bulls in 2026-27 wins over replacement player.

The problem, at least for now, is absolutely dreadful defense when Josh Giddey (10.4 points and 8.5 assists), Norman Powell (21.1 points), Matas Buzelis (13.7 points) and Wilson (18.9 points and 6.2 rebounds) are all on the floor.

The length at every spot outside Powell's hasn't made up for a lack of attentiveness. And Buzelis and Wilson appear years (or at least months) away from the ability to reliably stay in front of wings.

It also doesn't help that Giddey, Buzelis and Wilson are all below average from three (and Powell is barely average himself), but it's the defense that's really dooming this group.

28. Sacramento Kings: Acuff, LaVine, Hunter, Achiuwa, Sabonis

The Sacramento Kings are still a full-scale disaster. And with this particular group, it's hard to decide if it's the offense or defense that's the bigger problem.

Individually, Zach LaVine (21.4 points and a 39.1 three-point percentage), Domantas Sabonis (14.5 points, 3.8 offensive rebounds and a 64.6 field-goal percentage) and Darius Acuff (27.4 points, 8.4 assists and a 38.0 three-point percentage over his last eight games) have been good, but Sacramento is only scoring 104.1 points per 100 possessions when all three are on the floor.

For whatever reason, Acuff's high-volume scoring isn't jelling with Sabonis, LaVine, De'Andre Hunter and Precious Achiuwa, but it's hard to argue that the statistical issues are his fault.

The Kings' offensive rating, effective field-goal percentage and turnover percentage are all better when Acuff is on the floor.

The answer may be the same as it's been for a couple years now: It's probably time to trade LaVine and Sabonis.

27. Charlotte Hornets: Schröder, Brandon Miller, Sion James, Reid, Diabaté

This group's respectable record mostly came in the opening days of the season, when they beat the Brooklyn Nets, Washington Wizards and Miami Heat before they started clicking.

And it didn't take long for the same lineup's numbers to fall off a cliff. In the next three games it started, Charlotte averaged just 90.7 points per game.

That speaks to an offense that has been genuinely terrible all season. And without LaMelo Ball setting everyone up, it's getting harder and harder to see the path to mediocrity on that end.

Moussa Diabaté (8.7 points and 5.5 offensive rebounds) and Naz Reid (17.3 points, 8.5 rebounds and a 35.6 three-point percentage) have been solid, though head coach Charles Lee has already benched Reid for a second half, saying he was not meeting team standards. Reid later said their relationship was " fine ."

And Brandon Miller (20.6 points and a 26.0 three-point percentage), Dennis Schröder (10.2 points and a 20.0 three-point percentage) and Sion James (6.0 points and a 25.9 three-point percentage) have all been somewhere between underwhelming and flat-out bad.

Kon Knueppel looks like he could be a star, but he's not the kind of offensive engine that can fix all of that as soon as he gets back.

26. Phoenix Suns: Green, Booker, Brooks, Bridges, Maluach

It's worth noting that Oso Ighodaro is one start away from bumping Khaman Maluach from this analysis. And the same lineup with Ighodaro at the 5 is 4-1. That group is still getting killed in its minutes, though. So, the breakdown isn't dramatically different.

What it comes down to, ultimately, is poor play from Jalen Green (11.8 points with a 46.2 effective field-goal percentage), poor shooting from Miles Bridges (14.6 points with a 30.6 three-point percentage) and poor defense from both.

Devin Booker (25.5 points, 5.0 assists and a 37.5 three-point percentage) is playing like a star, and Dillon Brooks (14.9 points, while shooting 43.1 percent from deep) is hitting shots, but replacing Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale with Bridges and more availability from Jalen Green has swapped grit and reliable shooting for complacency and lots of bricks.

25. Indiana Pacers: Smith, Nembhard, Nesmith, Siakam, Zubac

For a second consecutive season, the Indiana Pacers have been hit hard enough with injuries that it probably doesn't even make sense to analyze their "starting five." We've barely seen it.

The Pacers have already tried eight different groups. Tyrese Haliburton isn't in the most-used one. He has been in four different ones.

But the group listed above features four of the five players in the presumed starting five from the preseason. And its net rating is a pretty good illustration of how important Haliburton is.

24. Toronto Raptors: Quickley, Walter, Barrett, Barnes, Poeltl

The Toronto Raptors have almost too many injuries to be able to analyze them at all.

Kawhi Leonard has only played in two games, and now Scottie Barnes (23.5 points, 7.6 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 2.3 steals) is out with an adductor injury.

There isn't a ton to say about a team's starting lineup when its two best players have missed this much time.

And if the rest of the starters don't start producing a little better before they return, having a healthy roster may not matter all that much.

RJ Barrett (21.3 points with a 30.2 three-point percentage) and Immanuel Quickley (17.6 points, while shooting 32.1 percent from three) both have to shoot better. And Jakob Poeltl (8.3 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.8 blocks) could give them a little more juice as a passer and shot-blocker (two things he's done better in the past).

23. Miami Heat: Mitchell, Thompson, Wiggins, Antetokounmpo, Adebayo

It's not hard to see why the Miami Heat have already moved on from Andrew Wiggins as a starter.

On the season, he's averaging just 8.8 points, while shooting 32.0 percent from deep. And since Miami moved him to the bench, it's 4-0, with just about everyone left in the starting five looking better.

In those four games, Giannis Antetokounmpo is averaging 32.5 points, 12.0 rebounds and 4.3 assists, Bam Adebayo is at 21.5 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists, Klay Thompson is averaging 20.0 points while shooting 44.1 percent from three, and Davion Mitchell is adding 18.3 points and 11.3 assists.

Replacing Wiggins with Pelle Larsson, who's shooting better and does more with the ball in his hands, has been transformative for this group.

22. Portland Trail Blazers: Henderson, Lillard, Camara, Avdija, Clingan

Having to use this lineup for the Portland Trail Blazers is seriously testing the rule to go with the most-used starting five for each team.

For one thing, it only has that spot because of Ja Morant's injury. For another, it's already been scrapped. For obvious reasons (see the net rating above), Scoot Henderson was recently sent back to the bench, and it's hard to imagine him getting back into the first five any time soon.

In his five starts, Henderson averaged 9.2 points and 1.0 assists (as a nominal point guard), while shooting 42.1 percent on twos and 21.1 percent on threes.

And perhaps most damning, when Damian Lillard (20.6 points and 4.3 assists), Toumani Camara (13.2 points with a 43.6 three-point percentage), Deni Avdija (23.9 points, 6.3 assists and 6.1 rebounds) and Donovan Clingan (11.0 points, 10.5 rebounds and 2.2 blocks in 25.3 minutes, while shooting 43.3 percent from three) are on the floor without Henderson, Portland is plus-27.3 points per 100 possessions.

21. Los Angeles Clippers: Garland, Dunn, Jones, Hachimura, Jackson

The Los Angeles Clippers are doing plenty of losing this season, but it doesn't appear to be the fault of this starting lineup, at least not entirely.

Sure, it would be nice if the first five won its minutes by more, but winning them at all is a plus. And they're doing it with pretty solid, versatile defense.

Kris Dunn (7.9 points, 4.5 assists and 2.1 steals), Derrick Jones (11.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks), Rui Hachimura (13.6 points and 1.1 steals) and Isaiah Jackson (5.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.2 steals) are all reliable on that end.

And Darius Garland (20.7 points and 6.9 assists, while shooting 36.0 percent from deep) is doing just enough to set everyone up on offense.

This obviously isn't the league's most inspiring starting five, but it's also far from a disaster.

20. Milwaukee Bucks: Rollins, Herro, Jaquez, Kuzma, Turner

The Milwaukee Bucks have plenty of problems, but this particular starting five (which the team already gave up on) isn't one of them.

Despite the poor production and lowlight reels of Myles Turner just wandering the floor, this lineup's combination of playmaking from Ryan Rollins, Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez and solid defense from the whole group helped it comfortably win its minutes.

When all five are on the floor, per 75 possessions, Herro averages 28.6 points and 5.0 assists, Kuzma averages 22.4 points and Jaquez averages 20.5 points and 3.1 assists, while Rollins adds 6.6 assists and Turner pitches in with 3.9 blocks.

19. Orlando Magic: Black, Richardson, Bane, Wagner, Carter

This obviously isn't Orlando's regular starting five, but Paolo Banchero getting hurt in the second game of the season knocked him out of the mix for now.

And although Franz Wagner (24.4 points, 8.3 assists, 6.8 rebounds and 1.3 steals) has filled the role of alpha well, this particular group still isn't working for a few reasons.

For one thing, although Wagner's net rating swing (the difference in the team's point differential per 100 possessions when a player is on or off the court) is off-the-charts positive, his 26.6 three-point percentage is contributing to a ho-hum offense. Jase Richardson shooting 22.2 percent isn't helping, either.

This lineup's turnover percentage is another problem. On the year, Wagner is averaging 4.3 turnovers in 36.8 minutes, while Anthony Black is adding another 3.1 in 32.1 minutes.

To take better advantage of the shooting numbers of Desmond Bane (18.3 points with a 40.9 three-point percentage), Black (16.3 points with a 40.0 three-point percentage) and Wendell Carter Jr. (13.5 points with a 40.0 three-point percentage), this group has to take better care of the ball.

18. Brooklyn Nets: Traoré, Johnson, Porter, Randle, Sharpe

We may still think of the Brooklyn Nets as a young, inexperienced team, but this particular lineup actually has a fair bit of experience.

Michael Porter Jr.'s (21.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and a 37.5 three-point percentage) shooting and Julius Randle's (19.9 points, 6.3 rebounds and 5.0 assists) slashing complement each other well. And Day'Ron Sharpe (8.8 points, 7.2 rebounds and 4.2 assists) is one of the more underrated passing bigs in the league. That's a skill-position combo that can really open up an offense.

If Nolan Traoré (12.7 points, 2.5 assists and a 41.9 three-point percentage) keeps shooting the way he is and Chaney Johnson keeps defending well, this is a group that could keep Brooklyn in games.

17. New Orleans Pelicans: Fears, Jones, Murphy, Williamson, Matković

There's a major small-sample caveat here, as this lineup has only started three games and played 39 minutes together, but it's not hard to see why it seems to be working.

Zion Williamson (21.9 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.7 assists) is flanked by a couple shooters in Trey Murphy III (15.6 points and a 37.7 three-point percentage) and Karlo Matković (42.5 percent from deep). Jeremiah Fears (15.3 points and 5.2 assists) is able to get to the paint and is setting up teammates well. And Herbert Jones and Murphy bring switchable, lengthy defense all over the floor.

Like just about everyone else, this group's availability has been heavily impacted by injuries. But if it gets more time together, New Orleans should be more competitive.

16. Dallas Mavericks: Irving, Martin, Flagg, Washington, Gafford

It's easy to be excited about the Dallas Mavericks right now.

Though the net rating above is underwhelming, the Mavs are plus-6.8 points per 100 possessions when Cooper Flagg (24.1 points, 7.0 rebounds, 6.4 assists and 2.0 steals) and Kyrie Irving (22.7 points and 4.4 assists, while shooting 39.8 percent from three) are on the floor.

And in this particular lineup, they're surrounded by plenty of veteran know-how, length and defensive versatility from Caleb Martin (1.9 assists in 20.2 minutes), P.J. Washington (13.9 points and 6.9 rebounds) and Daniel Gafford (9.2 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 21.2 minutes).

15. Washington Wizards: Young, Dybantsa, George, Davis, Sarr

This is a good example of how deceptive a team's record with a given starting five can be.

The Washington Wizards may have lost all but one of the games they've started this way, but this lineup itself is doing just fine. Defensively, it's excellent.

When these five are on the floor, Washington is surrendering just 99.4 points per 100 possessions, a near-phenomenal number for a lineup with Trae Young (19.7 points and 8.8 assists, but a 47.2 effective field-goal percentage).

The reasons they're able to cover for the often spacey Young are pretty clear. There is tons of length and athleticism all over the rest of this lineup with Anthony Davis (25.6 points and 10.5 rebounds), Alex Sarr (11.2 points and 7.4 rebounds), rookie AJ Dybantsa (15.0 points, 6.1 rebounds and 2.3 assists) and Kyshawn George (18.2 points, 4.8 assists, 4.5 rebounds and a team-high 1.2 blocks).

And George's breakout, specifically, makes it hard to not be high on Washington's potential to stay in the play-in mix. Having Young and AD put them there in most preseason prognostications, and George should keep them there despite a concerning start in the win-loss columns.

14. Cleveland Cavaliers: Harden, Mitchell, Watson, Mobley, Allen

With their continuity, their experience from multiple playoff runs and the addition of Peyton Watson (10.4 points, 2.7 assists and 1.5 blocks), this group was supposed to be one of the better starting fives in the league.

And this early in the season, there's still plenty of time for it to become that. One or two big stints could swing that net rating.

But right now, Watson's shooting struggles (he's at 21.3 percent from deep) and an apparent lack of intensity from Donovan Mitchell (23.0 points and 5.6 assists), James Harden (16.9 points and 5.8 assists), Evan Mobley (16.9 points and 7.3 rebounds) and Jarrett Allen (12.5 points and 8.3 rebounds) are dooming this lineup's minutes.

The clearest evidence of that may have come in Saturday's win over the Dallas Mavericks, when all five sat, and Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas led Cleveland to victory.

13. Atlanta Hawks: McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Daniels, Johnson, Okongwu

The Atlanta Hawks have already pivoted away from this lineup to start rookie Kingston Flemings over CJ McCollum (14.1 points and 4.0 assists), but the numbers were good enough with this group to think it could come back.

With Jalen Johnson (20.0 points, 8.8 rebounds and 7.5 assists) as the playmaking hub in the middle and neither Onyeka Okongwu (13.9 points, 7.9 rebounds and 2.7 assists) nor Dyson Daniels (9.5 points, 7.2 rebounds, 5.6 assists and a league-leading 2.9 steals) being a serious shooting threat, this lineup could really use the shooting of Nickeil Alexander-Walker (21.5 points and 3.7 threes) and McCollum.

Flemings is hitting his outside attempts at a higher rate, but his volume is significantly lower.

12. Detroit Pistons: Cunningham, Robinson, Thompson, Collins, Reed

Given the Detroit Pistons' overall record, and its record when starting games with this lineup, it's sort of hard to believe how bad that point differential is.

But, for whatever reason, minutes with Cade Cunningham (25.7 points and 7.9 assists) and John Collins (10.4 points and 6.0 rebounds) just don't seem to be working.

Both have negative net rating swings on the season. They also have a negative net rating as a duo, but Cunningham is in the black when sharing the floor with each of the other three listed above.

In theory, this lineup should, at the very least, be winning its minutes. It has a fringe MVP candidate, a lights-out shooter and one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA. But sometimes, one ill-fitting piece can throw off the whole.

11. New York Knicks: Brunson, Hart, Bridges, Anunoby, Towns

Typically, less than a month into the title defense, there couldn't be much reason for panic for the starting five that just won the championship.

But three of the New York Knicks' five starters have struggled enough to raise questions.

Jalen Brunson (26.6 points and 5.7 assists) and Karl-Anthony Towns (21.1 points, 13.7 rebounds and 3.7 assists) are their usually productive selves, but OG Anunoby, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges are shooting a combined 30.9 percent from three. And Hart and Bridges are averaging 7.3 and 6.9 points, respectively.

It may seem like an overreaction, given what he did to carry the Knicks to the title just a few months ago, but the answer may be to take the ball out of Brunson's hands a bit more, get it moving around the floor and empower everyone else to contribute.

10. Oklahoma City Thunder: Gilgeous-Alexander, McCain, Mitchell, Williams, Hartenstein

The Oklahoma City Thunder deserve a mountain of credit for the way they've fought through the loss of three starters (Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren), but the injuries finally appear to be catching up to them.

This group is just so light on playmaking beyond Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (30.5 points, 4.5 assists and 4.2 rebounds), and it's only scoring 108.7 points per 100 possessions.

Remarkably, all the absences haven't really cost them on the defensive end, though. Clearly, the culture extends beyond Williams, Wallace and Holmgren, because this lineup is still holding opponents to a well-below- average offensive rating.

9. Golden State Warriors: Curry, Green, Lendeborg, Podziemski, Santos

The obvious shame here is that Stephen Curry (27.8 points, 4.3 threes and 3.9 assists in 26.3 minutes) is out for the next several weeks, because the Golden State Warriors, when they had all five of the above available, looked dangerous. They looked "might even finish in the top six" dangerous.

That hope is certainly diminished now, but depending on how long Curry's oblique injury keeps him out of action, it doesn't have to be dashed.

The combination of Curry and Yaxel Lendeborg (20.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.5 assists and a 41.4 three-point percentage) alone is already among the most interesting in the league. The superstar's outside shooting and gravity open up the floor for everyone else. And Lendeborg's driving helps pull defenses toward the paint.

With those two surrounded by three solid gap-fillers in Brandin Podziemski (16.5 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.8 assists), Gui Santos (5.6 points and 3.9 rebounds) and Draymond Green (7.1 assists and 4.7 rebounds), this lineup was cruising before the Curry news derailed it.

8. Philadelphia 76ers: Maxey, Edgecombe, Brown, James, Embiid

The Philadelphia 76ers are winning games. That's more important than anything else you'll read in this blurb. But this suddenly star-laden starting five might actually be better off playing a little less together.

There's a good chance they'll get more used to playing together over the course of the season, but accommodating four players who are used to being (very) high-volume scorers is tough.

Some of the group's less efficient scorers (like Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown) may have to lean a little more toward playmaking to unleash the player who's undoubtedly their alpha.

Even while trying to figure out how to coexist with legends, Tyrese Maxey is averaging 26.7 points and 5.5 assists.

7. Memphis Grizzlies: Jerome, Coward, Wells, Boozer, Edey

The Memphis Grizzlies have lost half the games they've started with this lineup, but it's obviously not the reason why.

When Ty Jerome (25.4 points and 5.3 assists), Cameron Boozer (15.5 points, 9.7 rebounds and 5.2 assists), Cedric Coward (13.8 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists), Jaylen Wells (11.4 points and 2.1 threes) and Zach Edey (7.6 points, 7.7 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 20.7 minutes) are all on the floor, Memphis' defense is stifling.

And the scoring balance after Jerome is generating more than enough offense to dominate this group's minutes.

6. Denver Nuggets: Murray, Braun, Johnson, Gordon, Jokić

With Nikola Jokić (23.7 points, 10.5 rebounds and 9.1 assists, but a 58.8 true shooting percentage that's his lowest mark since 2015-16) and Aaron Gordon (11.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists) finally showing signs of age, the Denver Nuggets may not be a first-tier title contender, but the starting five is still one of the best units in the game.

Their dominance, as always, begins with the two-man game between Jokić and Murray (25.9 points, 6.2 assists and 3.6 threes, while shooting 49.4 percent from three), who just made history as the first teammates on record who each threw at least 1,000 assists to the other.

And surrounding that with the defense and cutting of Christian Braun (12.8 points and 2.2 steals) and Gordon, as well as the shooting of Cameron Johnson (12.1 points and 2.1 threes, with a 39.5 three-point percentage), makes this starting five especially difficult to handle.

5. Minnesota Timberwolves: Ball, Dosunmu, McDaniels, Kuminga, Gobert

When Anthony Edwards went to the injured list with a procedure on his knee, a decline for the Minnesota Timberwolves almost felt inevitable.

But this group has played absolutely devastating defense. Ayo Dosunmu, Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga can all guard multiple positions (and do it well). And Rudy Gobert is still one of the best defensive anchors in the NBA.

Add in just enough offense from the perimeter players over the nine games since Edwards went down, and you have a recipe for dominance.

In that stretch, Dosunmu is putting up 21.4 points and shooting 45.2 percent from deep, LaMelo Ball is averaging 20.3 points and 6.2 assists, and McDaniels is averaging 17.9 points and 4.2 assists.

4. Houston Rockets: VanVleet, Thompson, Durant, Smith, Şengün

Only three lineups in the NBA have logged more total minutes than the Houston Rockets' starters. And thanks mostly to a stifling defense, Houston is cruising in this group's minutes.

There is tons of length, switchability and athleticism between Amen Thompson (15.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.1 assists), Jabari Smith (15.9 points, while shooting 40.7 percent from three) and Kevin Durant (21.0 points and 3.8 assists).

They've more than made up for any shortcomings from Alperen Şengün (23.1 points, 9.6 rebounds, 7.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks) and Fred VanVleet (14.0 points and 5.4 assists) on that end, while Şengün has generated the attack and VanVleet has stabilized it on the other.

3. Boston Celtics: White, George, Tatum, Walsh, Robinson

This group actually hasn't played a ton together, because Jordan Walsh has been something of a nominal starter. He's averaging just 16.2 minutes per game this season and only 18.2 in his starts.

Still, the other four here fit together well enough to warrant this lofty ranking and consideration for the Boston Celtics as serious title contenders.

Paul George (22.0 points and 3.8 assists, while shooting 44.0 percent from deep), with his willingness to be a floor spacer and keep the ball moving, has fit like a glove in his first year. Derrick White's (12.8 points and 5.3 assists) playmaking and defense continue to make him one of the league's best glue guys. And Mitchell Robinson (5.6 points and 5.4 rebounds), who's barely playing more than Walsh and hasn't started a game since October, is dominating the boards when he's on the floor.

But ultimately, this season and this lineup are about Jayson Tatum's ascension to true alpha status. Statistically, he's been there for several years, but there was still an erroneous perception that Boston had sort of a 1A/1B situation with Tatum and Jaylen Brown. The latter is gone now, and Tatum is averaging 26.3 points, 7.5 assists and 6.1 rebounds in his absence.

2. Los Angeles Lakers: Dončić, Reaves, LaRavia, Thybulle, Kessler

The Los Angeles Lakers' most-used starting five is absolutely dominating its competition.

And while Luka Dončić (38.6 points, 7.6 assists, 7.5 rebounds and 2.0 steals) deserves the lion's share of the credit, he's not responsible for that gaudy net rating alone.

Austin Reaves' (24.7 points and 4.7 assists) secondary playmaking and Walker Kessler's (14.5 points, 10.8 rebounds and 2.2 blocks) rim protection and rim running have been vital.

And Jake LaRavia (52.2 percent from three) and Matisse Thybulle (2.2 steals in 24.4 minutes) have been excellent gap-fillers.

1. San Antonio Spurs: Fox, Harper, Castle, Vassell, Wembanyama

It's hard to argue with the results. The San Antonio Spurs made a way-ahead-of-schedule run to the Finals with Dylan Harper coming off the bench last season.

But it's been abundantly clear for close to a calendar year that the Spurs needed to start all three of their star guards together. This season, they have.

And that trio, along with Devin Vassell (11.5 points and 3.0 assists) and MVP candidate Victor Wembanyama (28.8 points, 11.7 rebounds, 4.2 blocks, 3.1 assists and 1.2 steals in 29.3 minutes), is just annihilating opponents.

Stephon Castle (15.4 points and 5.1 assists) is big and athletic enough to play some nominal 3. De'Aaron Fox's (13.6 points and 5.8 assists) speed keeps defenses off-balance. And Dylan Harper's (17.3 points and 4.8 assists) change-of-pace ability and finishing make him a nightmare assignment.

There's no way for an opposing defense to know where the attack is going to come from, and that's not even this lineup's biggest strength.

The switchability of Harper, Castle and Vassell, backed by Wembanyama's generational rim protection, gives this lineup a terrifying defense.

articles.title: New Zion Trade Rumors Leak on His 'Behavior,' Market and LaMelo Ball Impact After Dejounte's Request
articles.summary: If the New Orleans Pelicans wanted to make a major pivot, this might be the point to consider parting ways with two-time All-Star Zion Williamson.
articles.body:
If the New Orleans Pelicans wanted to make a major pivot, this might be the point to consider parting ways with two-time All-Star Zion Williamson.

New Orleans is 4-10 to open the 2026-27 NBA season, and veteran guard Dejounte Murray formally requested a trade. ESPN insiders Brian Windhorst and Tim MacMahon discussed the team's situation in the newest episode of the Hoop Collective podcast .

MacMahon reported at the 12:30 mark that some within the NBA are wondering whether Williamson, like Murray, will press the issue and seek an exit. He went on to add New Orleans could have some leverage in negotiations.

"I will tell you this, Zion is in shape. Zion is performing well," MacMahon said. "The Pelicans have a lot of problems, Zion has not been one of them. And one might say then that makes this the perfect time for the Pelicans to explore the market for Zion."

Williamson is averaging 21.9 points on 60.2 percent shooting along with 5.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.9 steals. He has suited up in 13 of the Pelicans' 14 games.

Windhorst reported Williamson's performance on the court is matched by his effort behind the scenes. The 6'6" forward is "on his absolute best behavior" (13:27 mark).

"Showing up on time, coming to camp in reasonable shape, playing hard, showing support of his teammates, basically checking all the boxes," Windhorst said. "He's on his best behavior."

Teams rarely get equal value back when they're trading away star-level talent, though, and Williamson has faced persistent questions about his durability and conditioning .

As a result, New Orleans may have to settle for a return that's a little underwhelming. MacMahon cited the LaMelo Ball trade as one possible outcome for the Pels.

In a deal that included four teams , the Charlotte Hornets jettisoned Ball and got back Naz Reid, Mouhamadou Gueye, and draft capital. They received the Minnesota Timberwolves' 2033 first-round pick, second-rounders in 2029, 2032 and 2033, and three first-round pick swaps.

All things considered, it was a good move for Charlotte without being a total home run. Reid is already garnering trade speculation , and all of the NBA's changes to the draft lottery make it tough to project out the value of first-round picks.

We've come a long way from Williamson being floated as a chip in a blockbuster Kevin Durant trade. His stock has steadily declined, and there isn't as much hidden upside for a player who turned 26 in July.

It's unlikely New Orleans could flip Zion for another All-Star or a young player to orient the franchise around. However, this wouldn't be a pure salary dump and would allow for the front office to transition to a new phase.

articles.title: 'Distressed Asset,' Dejounte Murray's Trade Value Revealed in New NBA Rumors on Pelicans Star
articles.summary: After New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray's trade request was announced last week, it doesn't sound like teams around the NBA are in a rush to acquire him.
articles.body:
After New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray's trade request was announced last week, it doesn't sound like teams around the NBA are in a rush to acquire him.

During Monday's episode of The Hoop Collective , ESPN's Brian Windhorst revealed that Murray trade value has diminished, with other teams hoping to add extra assets to take on the veteran guard.

"They sent him home. And there's some audio that got out from some courtside microphones from a couple of days ago; I can't confirm what Dejounte, who he was talking about. People have jumped to conclusions, and I'm not saying it's wrong, but it seemed like it's a possibility that Dejounte was becoming hard to have around the team," Windhorst said at the 6:50 mark.

"So, in my discussions with teams over the last couple of days," he continued, "multiple teams have told me that they view, as [Tim MacMahon] just described, I mean, this is your opinion, but it is an informed opinion, because multiple teams have told me that they view Dejounte as a distressed asset to the point where if you were to trade for him that you would want compensation in addition to him to take him."

The Pelicans confirmed on Friday that they received Murray's trade request and will "evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization."

NBA insider Chris Haynes reported that the Phoenix Suns "have registered interest" in acquiring Murray. However, NBA insider Marc Stein noted that it's "not yet clear" how quickly a trade would materialize.

Murray can be a reliable floor general in the right situation, but it appears that he could have to wait a while before getting the chance to showcase his skills with another team.

articles.title: Latest NBA Rumors on Las Vegas Expansion as New Arena Eyed for NBA Summer League, USA Basketball
articles.summary: One ownership group seeking to bring an NBA expansion franchise to Las Vegas has wider plans for a new arena in Sin City, according to The Athletic's Mike Vorkunov and Joe Vardon.
articles.body:
One ownership group seeking to bring an NBA expansion franchise to Las Vegas has wider plans for a new arena in Sin City, according to The Athletic's Mike Vorkunov and Joe Vardon .

Vorkunov and Vardon reported the group, which is fronted by Vegas Golden Knights owner Bill Foley, has interest in staging USA Basketball and NBA Summer League games at a new arena in the city.

The Vegas Summer League splits games between Thomas & Mack Center and the adjacent Cox Pavilion. Shifting the event to a different venue wouldn't present a lot of logistical challenges.

USA Basketball is stationed in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and the organization is reportedly "not seeking to move." Colorado Springs isn't where the national team stages its games, though, so it could make sense to turn Vegas a dedicated host city.

Building a new arena is likely to be a challenge , though.

Construction of the Athletics' new stadium in Las Vegas is ongoing and resulted from a long, divisive saga. Local residents might push back even more on a new basketball venue.

T-Mobile Arena, which is used by the NHL's Golden Knights, is only 10 years old and has a capacity of 18,000 seats for basketball games. Foley suggested this past summer he's prepared to make the necessary renovations to get the arena more suitable for NBA games.

"We believe we can spend $300, $400 million to improve T-Mobile and add roughly 1,000 seats, more suites, and make it NBA-ready when the NBA does decide to come," he told the Las Vegas Review-Journal 's Mick Akers . "It may not be the home forever for the Golden Knights and the NBA team, but it certainly is going to be an excellent place for them, for both teams to play, for several years in the future."

That plan would cost less and take less time than constructing a new arena from scratch.

This could all be a moot issue, with Vorkunov and Vardon noting two other ownership groups are in the running. The presumed leaders are Nancy Walton Laurie, who's the daughter of Walmart co-founder Bud Walton, and husband Bill Laurie.

articles.title: Ty Jerome's absence looms large as Grizzlies visit Wizards and 76ers take on Nets in NBA action
articles.summary: Joel Embiid is a game-time decision as the Philadelphia 76ers visit the Brooklyn Nets, with the under 226.5 favored in a matchup of bottom-half offenses.
articles.body: The NBA is already about 20% complete, which is almost crazy to think about. The NBA Cup has had some real traction, and we've had some fun surprises in the early season. There are some teams I'm wondering about - will they keep their hot start going, and will others turn it around? I have two different looks for tonight and think both should cash for us. 76ers vs. Nets The Philadelphia 76ers are one of the teams that have put together a hot start, but I don't think anyone really should be surprised. They have a strong group of players in their starting lineup. The big question is whether they can compete with and beat the best teams in the league. How will they manage playing against the Nuggets, Cavs, Knicks, Spurs, and other squads in a seven-game series? Also, health will always be an issue. Joel Embiid hurt himself again recently, and he is a game-time decision in this one. The Brooklyn Nets are terrible this season, something that also should've been expected. They are 3-9 for the season and just 1-3 in the Barclays Center. Their team is figuring things out to a certain extent. Michael Porter Jr. remains their best scoring option, but just because he can put the ball in the bucket doesn't mean he can translate that into wins for his squad. Julius Randle has always been mostly an isolation player, and finding the right fit for him and players around him has always been a bit of a challenge. Neither of these teams are scoring a ton of points this year. The 76ers average just 112.6 points per game, and the Nets are at just 110.2. Both are in the bottom half of the league. Defensively, the 76ers are ranked 9th in the league. Brooklyn is 21st. Philadelphia is coming off a home stand and played yesterday. The Nets are coming off a road trip, but do have a bit of a rest advantage. I lean toward Philly covering the -5.5. However, I'm taking the under 226.5 here, as I think both teams coming into Brooklyn for the game will struggle with scoring. Grizzlies vs. Wizards The Memphis Grizzlies have been one of the bigger surprises of this season; the team is 9-4 for the season and hasn't lost a road game this year. Memphis being good wasn't something I expected, and most of it should be attributed to Ty Jerome looking like an All-Star this season. Jerome has averaged 25.4 points per game. Cam Boozer has transitioned well to the NBA game and is averaging almost a double-double for the team. The Washington Wizards are a team that has struggled to find their footing. This is a bit surprising to me, as their roster is actually pretty deep. They have more than enough pieces to be good; they just aren't. Anthony Davis looks good; Trae Young is averaging about nine assists and 18 points per game. I'm looking forward to seeing how AJ Dybantsa evolves. He is averaging 15.1 points and six rebounds per game. Jerome will be out for this game, and he is the only player averaging 20 or more points this season for the team. The Wizards are at home and have the better players, but they've also lost seven straight games. articles.title: Kyrie Irving Talks Criticism from Playing with LeBron James, Cavs' 2016 Championship vs. Warriors
articles.summary: Despite Saturday's loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers, Dallas Mavericks star point guard Kyrie Irving found a moment to reflect on his time with his first franchise.
articles.body:
Despite Saturday's loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers, Dallas Mavericks star point guard Kyrie Irving found a moment to reflect on his time with his first franchise.

The Cavs were celebrating their 2016 NBA championship during Saturday's game, and the 2011 No. 1 pick acknowledged how former teammate LeBron James impacted his career.

"They like to say, 'He's not a winner. He didn't do anything without Bron,'" Irving said after scoring 34 points in Dallas' 127-117 loss, per The Athletic's Christian Clark . "I think it's all in fair criticism. But as I look at it, it was just me being a young player in the league. I needed some veterans around me. I needed some good pieces. I needed to be battle-tested. I feel like that's what prepared me for the moments I'm in right now."

Irving wasn't able to lead the Cavs to the playoffs until James returned to Cleveland in 2014. The duo led the franchise to its first championship after completing a historic 3-1 series comeback against the Golden State Warriors in the 2016 NBA Finals.

"Fifty-two years is a long time to be waiting for a championship, and we did it," Irving said. "I think that's one of the hardest championships ever in NBA history, and we got to accomplish it."

Now, Irving is the veteran leader of a 7-7 Mavs team that is riding a three-game losing streak into Wednesday's game against the Golden State Warriors. The 34-year-old has been off to a strong start this year after missing all of last season with a torn ACL, and he will try to help Dallas end its skid when the team returns to action.

articles.title: Blake Griffin admits NBA players would clown Stephen A. Smith, Skip Bayless debates for being ‘dead wrong’ about everything
articles.summary: Though made for entertainment, Stephen A. Smith and Skip Bayless’ First Take debates were great material for NBA players like Blake Griffin. Speaking to GQ,...
articles.body:
Though made for entertainment, Stephen A. Smith and Skip Bayless ' First Take debates were great material for NBA players like Blake Griffin .

Speaking to GQ, Griffin said that some players would watch First Take when Smith and Bayless were in their heyday because they were "both dead wrong."

Players didn't really believe either of the First Take analysts were even close on the points they were making. That prompted Griffin to create his show, The Stepback, which gives fans a show they can "rely on what's being said."

Griffin was then asked if he had heard from Smith after going after him during the premiere episode of his show. He hadn't, but he defended why he's so "hard" on him. He is "specific" with his criticisms, which he believes is fair. Griffin wasn't making blanket statements or generalizing his critiques.

During the first episode of The Stepback, Griffin took aim at Smith's feud with Tyrese Haliburton during the 2025 NBA Finals, likening him to a "movie villain." He said that Smith made "himself part of the story" as if he's an "action bad guy in a movie."

Smith and Bayless haven't consistently been opponents on First Take in years. Bayless left ESPN after a dozen years with the network in 2016. His last appearance on First Take was on June 21, 2016.

Bayless jumped ship for FOX Sports 1 after leaving ESPN in September 2016. He launched Skip and Shannon: Undisputed with Shannon Sharpe, a First Take-like debate show. He left FOX Sports 1 in August 2024.

However, he would return to First Take in May 2026 in what was initially a one-off reunion . He was then given a recurring slot on the show in September 2026, appearing during the final Friday of every month. The duo would also make appearances on Mad Dog's Sports Radio show on SiriusXM.

articles.title: AP College Basketball Poll 2026 Week 3 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: Michigan State and Texas Tech gained some ground in the newest Associated Press Top 25 poll thanks to some big wins last week.
articles.body:
Michigan State and Texas Tech gained some ground in the newest Associated Press Top 25 poll thanks to some big wins last week.

The Spartans took down Duke, which had been No. 2, while the Red Raiders upset previously third-ranked Illinois. They're now No. 2 and 9, respectively, in the updated rankings.

Kansas was also a big mover, jumping four spots to 11th after hammering Kentucky by 20 points.

In general, last week provided little in the way of big surprises.

Gonzaga suffered the largest upset. The Zags were up double digits on LSU midway through the second half but couldn't seal the deal and lost 81-80 in Spokane. A missed free throw by Davis Fogle allowed Donovan Dent to drill a go-ahead three-pointer in the waning moments.

Gonzaga coach Mark Few identified rebounding as a critical part of LSU's comeback.

"We'd get a stop on the first action and then they'd just pin their ear back and we couldn't get an offensive rebound at the end, including a huge one on a free throw, which we've worked on a lot," he told reporters .

Gonzaga has a few games to get things right before it heads to Anaheim, California, on Dec. 5 to play UCLA.

The Bulldogs at least still have a Top 25 ranking. That can't be said of Kentucky after a brutal week.

As frustrated as their fans will have been after the Kansas loss, only beating Northern Arizona by one point at home might've been worse. Coach Mark Pope's postgame message of "I hope everybody at Rupp had fun" didn't exactly resonate with people in Lexington.

Pope is midway through his third season at the helm. It's still too early to draw broad conclusions about his tenure, and there's a long way to go in 2026-27. You wouldn't be wrong, however, for suggesting the Wildcats are showing little in the way of progress.

Kentucky has non-conference games against Indiana, Virginia, Louisville and North Carolina ahead. Things could either be much better or get very, very worse before SEC play begins.

As fate would have it, Illinois and Duke cross paths on Tuesday night in Durham, North Carolina. If anything, their losses only heightens the stakes of this encounter as both schools will be itching to earn a statement win.

Also on Tuesday, Michigan State heads to Knoxville for a tough test against Tennessee. The Spartans may have a credible case for the No. 1 spot if they're 6-0 by the time next week's poll is revealed.

Granted, the same could be said of UConn if they beat Arizona on the road on Wednesday night and improve their record to 5-0.

articles.title: Men's basketball AP poll: Florida holds at the top while Michigan State jumps to No. 2 after big win over Duke
articles.summary: Florida is still undefeated, while Penny Hardaway is trying his hardest to get off the hot seat in Memphis.
articles.body:
Tom Izzo proved his group belongs this past week.

Michigan State rolled to a pretty convincing win over Duke at the State Farm Champions Classic last week, thanks to a huge outing from star guard Jeremy Fears. The Spartans led nearly the entire way during the contest in Chicago while shutting the Blue Devils down in an outcome not many had expected entering the week. Duke was a known national title favorite, and Michigan State was widely seen as a close step behind.

While the Spartans didn't jump to No. 1 in the national poll on Monday afternoon, they did move up three spots to No. 2. They now only trail undefeated Florida, which started out as the top-ranked team in the preseason poll last month. Duke fell to No. 5.

Both UConn and Virginia moved up a spot to No. 3 and No. 4, respectively. The Huskies are undefeated after rolling past Ohio State on Friday and the Cavaliers are a perfect 5-0 after a narrow win over Maryland. UConn will face both No. 12 Arizona and No. 5 Duke in the next two weeks, however, and Illinois, Kansas and Virginia waiting next month.

Illinois fell seven spots to No. 10 after losing at Texas Tech last Tuesday, too. The Red Raiders, now No. 9 in this week's poll, held on late after leading by as many as 22 to grab the win. They've now won 50 straight non-conference home games dating back to 2020.

Michigan State doesn't have much time to relax. After a blowout win over Northern Iowa, the Spartans will travel to take on No. 14 Tennessee next on Tuesday night. They'll have to take on No. 20 Arkansas next week, too, and will have No. 22 Gonzaga on their schedule before Big Ten play gets going.

But Izzo got his statement win early. He's still a very real threat in the Big Ten.

Memphis has been confusing so far this season. The Tigers opened the year with a very solid win over a then-ranked Iowa State on a neutral floor, and then they were blown out by No. 15 Vanderbilt early last week. The start didn't do much to get coach Penny Hardaway off the hot seat that he was very firmly on entering the 2026-27 campaign.

But on Sunday, they absolutely stunned Louisville. The Tigers, who fell into an 18-point hole in the first half, rallied to grab a 98-78 win over the Cardinals. Tylik Weeks dropped 24 points in that outing while the Tigers shot 58% from the field and 50% from behind the arc. Put simply, they looked great.

But the win still didn't quite move Memphis into the national rankings on Monday. They received 172 votes, which made them the No. 26 team in the country, just one spot outside of the official rankings. The loss for Louisville, its first of the season, moved it down 13 spots to No. 23.

Sunday's rally was great. But the question now is what that does for the Tigers. They have a relatively straightforward schedule the next few weeks, with big games against unranked Penn State and Baylor. Their only ranked game left before American play gets going is at No. 6 Texas on Dec. 16.

If Hardaway can lead his group into conference play with just a single loss, his group will not only be in a great position to make the NCAA tournament, but he'll be in a great spot to earn another season with the Tigers. Hardaway entered this season with just three NCAA tournament appearances in his eight seasons with the program, and they went just 13-19 last year. If they can't use Sunday's win to propel them forward over the next several weeks, Hardaway will certainly remain firmly on that hot seat he's been on for a while now.

But the win over Louisville — and entering the national conversation, even if it's one spot back — is certainly a good start.
